items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: we did, what was the other guy, Donovan, and we did some Beatles things

ctx.x: Yeah, “Changes” was I think the first one we did. And that was, we did a Phil Ochs’ tune, we did, what was the other guy, Donovan, and we did some Beatles things, some Lennon-McCartney tunes. And actually it was quite good. A lot of people still love that album. I mean I’ve had people tell me that they enjoyed it, especially younger people. And then the next one we did right after that was a thing called “Grass” and that was one that also had an electric piano, Roy played electric piano for a while because we…

Well one of the reasons I changed was that some of the clubs we were working had these terrible pianos. Like they have a baby grand, it’s five feet long, and it sounds like it’s strung with rubber bands, and there’s no music in it. You hit a note and it goes duh, instead of ding. So I said well the only thing I can do, I’ll get an electric piano, I’ll carry my own, it’ll be dependable, it’ll be in tune, I’ll have the same instrument to play on. So we did that. We had also a bunch of sound equipment.
